$description: Contextual Workspace capability navigation. The capability capsule IS the capability list: one horizontal row of entries, bounded in width, whose overflow strategy is internal scrolling rather than a menu. #1347 Capsule V2 supersedes the two rules this pattern previously carried — that direct chrome is bounded to the contextually-justified set, and that everything else is disclosed through More/menu. The bound the design keeps is on the capsule, not on the entry count: the capsule must remain inside the tool bar while its content scrolls. Membership is Nession's and does not vary with the work: a capability has a slot whenever it has a Workspace view, and state is drawn on the entry rather than expressed by its absence. An `unavailable` capability therefore keeps its slot, rendered *inert* — `disabled`, on `disabled-foreground`, the role the design system defines for a control the user cannot act with. Inert is not dead: the entry must read as inert rather than be a live control that silently does nothing, and it carries `data-capability-state` / `data-capability-presence` so its condition stays legible without the row changing membership. The active capability carries a selected state and is scrolled into view. Entries are labeled slots — icon over a name — so `wrap: true` is the honest claim: a long name (Claude Code) takes two lines inside its fixed-width slot, and the single-line guarantee lives on the slot's own line clamp rather than on the row's text. Each entry is one band tall (`capabilityEntryHeight`: 44px on App — the Conversation form's own `control-md` row — 40px on Web), and the glyph is drawn bare rather than as an icon button's painted circle. On App this puts both Capsule states at 56px total, which the relational assertion (SC-30) compares along with the shape, the radius and the placement. The row itself stays one horizontal row of slots. The capsule is present at every Workspace depth (owner decision 2026-10-03, superseding #1051's dock half): a pushed detail keeps the switcher, its own Back remains that depth's only leave, and every depth's scrollers spend the same measured capsule clearance so their last line can be brought above the bar. On App this band is one state of the same Capsule as the Terminal's Conversation form (owner decision 2026-10-03): the two share outer geometry — semantic radius, `control-md` vertical mass, the App dock's bottom/inset placement — and differ only in what the row contains. Its entries therefore take the standard App control band (`control.md` hit target, `control.visualSize` affordance) like every other Capsule control; the retired `touchTarget.compact` / `dockTarget` (28px) vocabulary existed for the old compact dock and is not protected.
